criteria: Factor the nonzero leading coefficient and add and subtract the matching square term.
Check the resulting identity by expansion and preserve the original expression for all allowed variable values.
set.description: For a real a!=0, rewrite a*x^2+b*x+c identically as a*(x+b/(2*a))^2+c-b^2/(4*a) by adding and subtracting the matching square term. This node covers the algebraic rewrite itself; solving an equation, interpreting a function graph, finding a circle center, and proving a bound are separate uses.
set.name: Completing the square in an expression

set.reason: Comparing prime exponents settles perfect-power and multiplicative equations. Linear or bounded integer equations are solved through divisibility, bounds or search, without unique factorization.

The first mastery criterion explicitly requires finding radical domains, and square roots are the central even-root case. Their nonnegative-radicand condition is exactly this source concept; only odd-root cases avoid it.

criteria: Identify radical domains and applicable sign constraints.
Check transformed candidates in the original equation.
set.description: Solve real equations with unknowns inside radicals, respecting even-root domains and signs; check candidates in the original equation after taking powers or substituting.
set.name: Solving real equations containing radicals
